A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Associative Transformer study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and relational-reasoning experiments, component ablations, attention analyses and Hopfield-energy measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds model configurations, comparison results, a test-time ablation and batch-wise energy measurements.

M1.justification: Equation 4 reverses the EWMA coefficients: with the unchanged alpha of 0.9, old/new memory weights change from 0.1/0.9 to 0.9/0.1. This changes the reported update rule, although the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or the equation was corrected. The core architecture and losses remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Triangle, Oxford-IIIT Pet and Sort-of-CLEVR with the same task coverage. Added model configurations and memory-forward controls do not introduce a new dataset or input scenario.

E2.justification: V2 adds Dense-Small and Dense-Base to the Sort-of-CLEVR comparison in Table 4 and ViT-Base to the Pet comparison in Figure 3. The earlier Pet label ViT-Small+GWL corresponds to AiT-Small, so that rename is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation of six-layer AiT-Medium, a test-time control disabling memory forward, and an average across relational/non-relational accuracy in Table 4. Existing dataset splits, preprocessing, batch sizes and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.5 tests whether current-batch memory forward helps retrieval, across classification and relational reasoning (Tables 7–8). Figure 11(b) additionally examines retrieved-pattern energy across training batches. Earlier component, initialization, temperature and attention-balance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means of three individual experiments in Section 5.1. V2 adds no seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or newly specified uncertainty-estimation procedure; additional curves do not establish a changed reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes AiT-Base CIFAR-100 accuracy from 59.10 to 60.78. Table 4 replaces AiT-Small's relational/non-relational scores of 67.74/99.60 with 76.82/99.85, reversing its relational ranking against Coordination (73.43), while remaining below CNN+RN (81.07). New Medium, dense-baseline, memory-forward and batch-energy results substantially extend the evidence. The numerical replacements are not explained as verified same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.7 extends the convergence argument from per-input energy reduction to an assertion that all patches reach their minima simultaneously and global energy is guaranteed to decrease. No proof is added, and the Hopfield energy and sparsity definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly claims in its contribution list to be the first work incorporating Hopfield networks into a sparse attention mechanism. V1 described its distinction from prior work without this categorical priority claim. The abstract and conclusion otherwise retain their core claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.8 replaces the earlier discussion of relational underperformance and difficulty reconstructing questions with a positive interpretation about spatial-relation learning. V2 also acknowledges beta-tuning sensitivity and distinguishes energy decrease within retrieval from energy variation as the memory changes across batches.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies frozen training memory shared across test batches, temporary current-batch retrieval updates, usually one Hopfield retrieval step, the replacement attention's query/key/value inputs, and the normalized question-embedding construction. These clarify previously underspecified implementation details; code availability remains a future promise.

R1.justification: V2 adds Awh et al. (2006), Gazzaley and Nobre (2011), and Baxter (2000) to support attention–memory and inductive-bias motivation, alongside the stronger priority claim. The principal related-work comparison and Appendix Table 5 remain intact; duplicated or consolidated references do not represent additional research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 revises the contribution list, condenses related-work and attention-analysis prose, expands implementation explanations, and adds a test-time appendix subsection. The main section sequence and most narrative content are preserved.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redraws the architecture diagram, adds the test-time schematic, expands the Pet plot and energy figure, and adds Tables 7–8. Table 4 gains rows and an average column, while several existing displays are resized or relocated. Earlier attention-balance figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The frozen-memory explanation and new memory-forward controls make the stateful evaluation easier to understand and assess. Additional model-size comparisons and clearer diagrams strengthen empirical support and communication. These are bounded gains: the changed AiT scores remain unexplained, and the stronger global-energy assertion receives no new proof.
